title.en: Mit, bei, nach and zu: everyday dative prepositions

summary.en: High-frequency prepositions like mit, bei, nach, and zu always trigger dative forms—including zum and zur.

body.en:
From season 1, episodes 1 and 2.

Checking into room four, Helga asks whether her window faces *zur Straße* or *zum Hof*. The next morning she asks *nach seinem Koffer* *mit dem Holzzug*, and Klara promises Werner that his secret is safe *bei uns*.

Prepositions in the core family *aus*, *bei*, *mit*, *nach*, *von*, and *zu* always take the dative case. In the singular, masculine and neuter *der* / *das* both shift to *dem* (*mit dem Holzzug*, *nach seinem Koffer*), while feminine *die* shifts to *der*.

In natural speech, *zu* merges with those articles into two indispensable shortcuts: *zu* + *dem* becomes *zum* (*zum Hof*), and *zu* + *der* becomes *zur* (*zur Straße*).

On replay, listen for how smoothly *zur Straße*, *zum Hof*, and *mit dem* flow as single rhythmic units.
